text:
A: Hello, love, can you hear me? I'm Joanne, from Gosport.
B: Yeah. Shazia. Walsall.
A: Oh, the Midlands. Erm, I never know how to start these. What do you do, Shazia?
B: Nothing at the minute. I'm at home with the kids. I used to pack at a warehouse but me back went.
A: Oh, I'm sorry. Backs are awful. Mine's not brilliant either, and my knees. I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school, have been for eleven years.
B: School kitchen? That's what I was thinking of doing. Once my youngest goes up to secondary. Dinner lady or a TA, something in school hours.
A: Oh, you'd be lovely at it! Honestly. It's term-time, so you get the holidays with your kids, that's the big thing.
B: Is it hard on your back, though? To be honest that's what I'm worried about.
A: Erm, I won't lie to you, love, it can be. It's the standing, and the lifting the big trays out of the oven, and then wiping all the tables in the hall after. Some days I go home and I can barely get up the stairs to my flat. But our cook's good, she'll swap me onto the till or the salad bit if I'm struggling. It depends on the school, really. I'd say ask them what the actual jobs are before you start. Sorry, I don't want to put you off.
B: No, that's helpful. Better you say it.
A: Have you got your food hygiene? That's the first thing they ask.
B: Yeah, I done it online. And first aid.
A: Well, there you go, you're halfway there already.
B: I started a childcare NVQ years ago. Never finished it. Had my first.
A: That's life, isn't it. How many have you got?
B: Three. Seventeen, fourteen and nine.
A: Oh, that's a houseful. I bet tea time's busy.
B: It's every day. I do curry, daal, chapatis, then the kids moan they want fish fingers. So I'm making two teas. And my mother-in-law comes round most afternoons, so that's another one.
A: Every afternoon?
B: Most. She's alright. She just sits there and tells me how to do things, d'you know what I mean.
A: Oh dear. Ha. My mum used to do that, God rest her. She'd stand at my cooker going "you want more salt in that".
B: Yeah. That's her.
A: Do you get a bit of time for yourself at all?
B: Dramas. Pakistani dramas on YouTube, at night. I'm hooked on one now, she's just found out her husband's been lying about everything.
A: Oh, I love a drama! I'm all crime ones and The Chase. And I do a bit of crochet, little hats for the baby unit at the hospital.
B: That's nice, that.
A: Thank you, love. I don't know if that's very interesting.
B: It is. More useful than me watching YouTube.
A: Oh no, we all need our telly. What do they eat at your house for a treat, then?
B: Chips from the chippy on a Friday, in a bap. Hamza won't have it any other way.
A: Friday fish and chips, same as me!
